task: Task 5: Add/delete rows — Скидки за количество (Increment 2)
summary: Task 5's diff (client/src/pages/Panel.jsx only) is well-scoped, correct, and confirmed working: npx vitest run passes (32/32) and npx vite build succeeds. The self-reported DeleteRowButton extension is genuinely additive/backward-compatible (verified against all 4 garment/operation call sites), the delete gate math is exactly settings.batch_discounts.length === 1, getDefaultDiscountRange pre-fills both min_qty and max_qty, and the render-time resync pattern is a correct, convergent instance of React's documented 'adjust state during render' idiom — no infinite-loop risk. One explicit AC bullet ('no changes to DeleteRowButton') was knowingly violated; the deviation is technically sound and transparently documented in decisions.md, so it is flagged as a minor/process finding rather than a code defect.

verified_claims.claim: 1. DeleteRowButton extension is backward-compatible with Tasks 3/4 call sites
verified_claims.evidence: grep for DeleteRowButton usages shows 4 garment/operation call sites (Panel.jsx:1291, 1314, 1360, 1386), each passing only isDeletable/onDelete. New props default to disabled=false, disabledHint="", so for these call sites: disabled={false} is a no-op HTML attribute, title/aria-label both evaluate to undefined (React omits undefined attrs). Rendered markup and behavior at these 4 sites is unchanged.

verified_claims.claim: 2. Discount disabled gate is exactly length === 1, wired to handleDeleteDiscount(index)
verified_claims.evidence: DiscountsBlock computes `canDeleteRow = settings.batch_discounts.length > 1;` and passes `disabled={!canDeleteRow}` to every row's DeleteRowButton, with `onDelete={() => handleDeleteDiscount(index)}`. !canDeleteRow is true iff length <= 1, and since the UI itself prevents the array reaching 0, this is effectively exactly length === 1 in practice, matching the AC bullet precisely. Not <=1 by accident, not >1 miswired — verified by reading the surrounding SettingsSection/.map block directly.

verified_claims.claim: 3. Add-form pre-fills both min_qty and max_qty via getDefaultDiscountRange
verified_claims.evidence: getDefaultDiscountRange (Panel.jsx:312-317, Task 2, unmodified) returns { min_qty: nextMinQty, max_qty: nextMinQty } — never a blank/zero max_qty. DiscountAddForm's initial useState and the handleAdd() post-submit refill both use the full object from this helper for both draft.min_qty and draft.max_qty. No regression of the historical 'max_qty left blank' bug.

verified_claims.claim: 4. Render-time state adjustment for resync is loop-safe
verified_claims.evidence: `if (suggestedMinQty !== defaultRange.min_qty) { setSuggestedMinQty(defaultRange.min_qty); setDraft(...) }` matches React's documented pattern for resetting state when a derived value changes (a tracked 'previous' value compared against the freshly-derived one, both updated together). getDefaultDiscountRange always returns a finite number (verified: falls back to 1 when tiers is empty/last tier's max_qty is non-finite), so the comparison converges to equality after exactly one extra render — no infinite loop. Verified this is also why the self-found bug (blank fields after add when defaultRange happened to equal the pre-add value) was possible under a naive useEffect-only design, and why the final code sidesteps it by computing the post-add refill synchronously from the just-added row rather than depending on the resync branch for the common case.

verified_claims.claim: 5. No changes to Task 2's handlers/constants beyond the additive DeleteRowButton extension, and no changes to Изделия/Усложнения sections
verified_claims.evidence: Full diff (198 lines, single file) reviewed end-to-end via `git show 9d05d6a -- client/`. Hunks are: (a) DeleteRowButton signature/JSX — additive only; (b) two DiscountsBlock call sites gaining handleAddDiscount/handleDeleteDiscount props (necessary, since those handlers live in the parent Panel component and DiscountsBlock is a module-scope sibling — documented in decisions.md as a forced, not chosen, deviation from 'call sites need no changes'); (c) DiscountsBlock body + new DiscountAddForm definition. handleAddGarment/handleDeleteGarment/handleAddOperation/handleDeleteOperation/handleAddDiscount/handleDeleteDiscount (Panel.jsx:891-937) and the Изделия/Усложнения JSX blocks are untouched by this diff.

findings.title: Explicit AC bullet ('no changes to Task 2's DeleteRowButton') was knowingly violated
findings.description: Task 5's own AC states: 'No changes made to Task 2's shared handlers/constants/DeleteRowButton'. The implementation extends DeleteRowButton with optional disabled/disabledHint props to satisfy the 'disabled, not hidden, for the last tier' requirement. The extension is technically well-executed (additive, verified backward-compatible, follows existing disabled: Tailwind conventions, includes title/aria-label for a11y) and the alternative — duplicating a second, locally-styled delete button inside DiscountsBlock to avoid touching Task 2's file at all — was considered and rejected in decisions.md as needless markup duplication that would have to be kept visually identical to the original. That tradeoff is defensible from a DRY/maintainability standpoint, but it is a genuine, not merely nominal, deviation from an unambiguous AC line, and the AC's wording suggests the task author anticipated and wanted the duplication path instead. Not a code defect — flagged so the deviation gets explicit sign-off (it is already documented in decisions.md) rather than being waved through on the strength of the self-report alone.
findings.recommendation: No code change required. Confirm this deviation is acceptable to the team lead/user given it's already surfaced in decisions.md; if a future task needs a third distinct DeleteRowButton state, prefer extending further over the alternative duplication path, since the extension approach has now been established as the project's convention here.

findings.title: Dead placeholder attributes on the always-controlled add-form inputs
findings.description: DiscountAddForm's min_qty/max_qty inputs set `placeholder={String(defaultRange.min_qty)}` / `placeholder={String(defaultRange.max_qty)}`, but `value={draft.min_qty}` / `value={draft.max_qty}` are always non-empty strings (pre-filled on mount and after every add) — the placeholder can never actually be shown to the user under normal operation. Harmless (defensive-looking, not incorrect), just slightly misleading to a future reader who might assume the field can go blank.
findings.recommendation: Optional cleanup: drop the placeholder props on min_qty/max_qty (keep it on percent, which is genuinely blank-able), or add a short comment noting they're defensive-only.
